Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $39. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item when I would have wanted it
2. Bidding more than my value could lead to a loss if I win
3. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, truthful bidding minimizes risk
4. The second-price auction mechanism rewards honest valuation
Therefore, I will bid my exact private value to maximize potential profit.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $27. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item even when I would profit
2. Bidding more than my value guarantees a potential loss
3. Bidding my exact value maximizes my potential profit
4. This strategy works regardless of other bidders' potential strategies
Since this is the only round, I'll follow the theoretically optimal approach.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $13. This is because:
1. If I bid less, I risk not winning when I could have profitably won
2. If I bid more, I risk paying more than my actual value
3. With values drawn independently each round, past rounds don't influence optimal strategy
4. The second-price auction mechanism incentivizes truthful bidding
Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value.
